svg.text: Every overlap between two sorted lists — stack and heap at every step
3 vs 2 spans → 2 overlaps · 6 comparisons vs 4 · 1 of 3 droppable
1 // primitive: len(xs) — element count. len(LEFT) = 3 · len(RIGHT) = 2
2 // primitive: LEFT / RIGHT — two lists of spans, each sorted and none overlapping its
6 // primitive: startOf(x) / endOf(x) — the two ends of a span.
8 // primitive: maxOf(a, b) / minOf(a, b) — the larger and smaller of two numbers.
10 // primitive: span(lo, hi) — one overlap. span(1, 3) = 1..3
11 // primitive: NONE — these two spans do not overlap at all.
14 // "Two sorted lists of time spans. Within a list, spans never overlap each other.
15 // Report every overlap between a LEFT span and a RIGHT one. 10^6 spans each. Then:
16 // both lists are streams that keep arriving — what may you throw away?"
18 // function: overlapOf(x, y) — the overlap, or NONE. Two lines, and they are the only
19 // geometry in the problem: it starts at the later start and ends at the earlier end.
28 // function: everyPair(left, right) — the answer everyone gives first: try all of them.
41 // function: sweep(left, right) — one pointer into each list. After testing a pair,
42 // advance whichever span ENDS FIRST: it cannot overlap anything further along the
43 // other list, because that list is sorted and its spans only start later.
59 // function: droppable(left, bound) — spans that can be forgotten, because nothing still
60 // to arrive on the other side can start before `bound`.
70 // function: main() — every pair, then the sweep, then what may be discarded.
73 val fast = sweep(LEFT, RIGHT) // 4 comparisons, same 2 overlaps
0x100 holds 1..3 130..245 540..540 and 0x200 holds 50..150 220..320. Two facts are handed to you and both matter: each list is **sorted**, and within a list
the spans **never overlap each other**. The second is what makes the advance rule below sound, and it is easy to read past as scene-setting.
